# Sirach Chapter 50 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 50 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 50 is the book's emotional and liturgical climax. Simon II (High Priest c. 219–196 BCE) was Ben Sira's contemporary — and the chapter's extended description of his emergence from the Holy of Holies and the performance of the temple liturgy (vv. 5–21) is our best literary eyewitness account of Second Temple worship. The extended simile sequence (vv. 6–10) is the most elaborate sustained comparison in the entire book and must be rendered with full poetic force.

**Key decisions:**
- vv. 6–10: The cascade of similes (morning star / full moon / sun / rainbow / rose / lily / frankincense / fire / incense / golden vessel / olive tree / cypress). Each simile must stand as a distinct image. Do not compress.
- v. 11: "as he came out from behind the curtain" — this is the emergence from the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur. The moment is charged with maximum drama.
- v. 12: "like a young cedar of Lebanon surrounded by the trunks of palm trees" — the High Priest surrounded by his brother priests. The image must be visually precise.
- v. 15: "the blood of the grape" for wine — preserve this phrase; it is a set idiom (Gen. 49:11; Deut. 32:14).
- v. 20: "he glorified himself in the name of the Lord" — this refers to the High Priest pronouncing the divine name (YHWH) aloud on Yom Kippur — the one day it was spoken.
- v. 25–26: The notorious anti-Samaritan passage. The "foolish people" at Shechem = Samaritans. Ben Sira's hostility must not be softened.
- v. 27: Ben Sira's colophon naming himself — preserve in full: "Jesus son of Sirach, son of Eleazar, of Jerusalem."

---

**50:1** Simon son of Onias the priest, who in his lifetime repaired the house and in his days fortified the temple;

**50:2** who laid the foundations for the high double walls, the lofty retaining walls of the temple court;

**50:3** who in his days had a reservoir hewn out — a cistern broad as the sea;

**50:4** who cared for his people against raiders and strengthened his city against enemies.

**50:5** How glorious he was when the people surrounded him as he came out from behind the curtain of the sanctuary!

**50:6** Like the morning star among the clouds, like the full moon on festival days,

**50:7** like the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High, like a rainbow gleaming in glorious clouds,

**50:8** like a flower of roses in the days of first fruits, like lilies at a spring of water, like a sprig of frankincense in the days of summer,

**50:9** like fire and incense in the censer, like a vessel of hammered gold adorned with every kind of precious stone,

**50:10** like an olive tree laden with fruit, like a cypress towering above the clouds —

**50:11** when he put on his glorious robe and clothed himself in the fullness of glory, as he went up to the holy altar, he filled the court of the sanctuary with his glory.

**50:12** When he received the portions from the hands of the priests, standing by the hearth of the altar, his brothers forming a crown all around him, he was like a young cedar of Lebanon in the midst of a ring of palm trunks.

**50:13** All the sons of Aaron in their splendor, with the Lord's fire offerings in their hands, before the whole congregation of Israel.

**50:14** Until he had completed the service of the altar and arranged the offering to the Almighty Most High,

**50:15** he stretched out his hand to the cup of libation and poured out wine from the blood of the grape; he poured it at the base of the altar, a pleasing aroma to the Most High, the King of all.

**50:16** Then the sons of Aaron shouted and sounded on their metal trumpets, and made a great sound to be remembered before the Most High.

**50:17** Then all the people together fell upon their faces to the ground to worship before the Most High, before the Holy One of Israel.

**50:18** The sound of singing rang out, and over the great multitude sweet melody arose.

**50:19** All the people of the land prayed and petitioned before the merciful Lord, until the worship of the Lord was completed and his service finished.

**50:20** Then he came down and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of Israel; the blessing of the Lord was upon his lips, and in the name of the Lord he glorified himself.

**50:21** And they bowed down a second time to receive the blessing from the Most High.

**50:22** And now bless the God of all, who does great things in every way, who exalts our days from the womb and deals with us according to his mercy.

**50:23** May he grant us gladness of heart, and may there be peace in our days in Israel, as the faithfulness of Israel endures forever.

**50:24** May his mercy remain with us always, and may he deliver us in our days!

**50:25** With two nations my soul is vexed, and the third is no nation at all:

**50:26** those who live on Mount Seir and the Philistines, and the foolish people who dwell in Shechem.

**50:27** Instruction in understanding and knowledge I have written in this book — I, Jesus son of Sirach, son of Eleazar, of Jerusalem — who poured out wisdom like rain.

**50:28** Blessed is he who meditates on these things; whoever lays them to heart will become wise.

**50:29** For if he does them, he will be strong for all things; for the light of the Lord is his path.
